WITH joined AS (
  SELECT pa.player_id, COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.bats), ''), '(blank)') AS bats_group
  FROM player_award pa
  JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pa.player_id
),
hand_counts AS (
  SELECT bats_group AS bats, COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) AS player_count
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY bats_group
),
totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) AS total_players FROM joined
),
shares AS (
  SELECT h.bats, h.player_count, h.player_count * 1.0 / t.total_players AS share
  FROM hand_counts h
  CROSS JOIN totals t
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares
)
SELECT s.bats, s.player_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS above_average_by
FROM shares s
CROSS JOIN avg_share a
WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
ORDER BY s.share DESC;

assumptions.assumption: Award records are the rows in player_award only (manager_award is excluded), and the inner join to player drops any award whose player_id has no match in player.
A blank hand is a bats value that is NULL, empty, or whitespace-only; these are grouped together under the label '(blank)'.
The share denominator is the count of distinct award-winning players across all matched awards, and each hand's share is its distinct player count divided by that total.
The average is the unweighted mean of the per-hand shares, and the 'above average' filter is strict (share > average).
The bats codes are not documented in the supplied context, so the query does not assume specific code values such as 'L', 'R', or 'B'.
